newsitem.title: CHINA: China jails former chief of top securities firm.
newsitem.headline: China jails former chief of top securities firm.

text.p: A Chinese court has sentenced the former head of a scandal-hit Shanghai securities house to 17 years in prison for embezzlement and accepting bribes, the Xinhua news agency said on Monday.

The Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate Court convicted Guan Jinsheng of accepting 294,000 yuan ($35,000) in bribes and misappropriating 2.4 million yuan in public funds between 1992 and 1994, the official agency said.

Guan Jinsheng was removed from his post as president of Shanghai International Securities Co after the brokerage was implicated in a huge bond futures trading scandal that rocked the Shanghai Stock Exchange in February 1995.

Xinhua did not mention the 1995 scandal in its report on Guan's conviction and did not elaborate on the charges against the former brokerage chief, who was once seen as the godfather of Shanghai's securities industry.
It gave no details of his movements since his removal.
In the 1995 trading scandal, Shanghai International took a position far exceeding the legal maximum in a bond futures contract and then tried to force down the market through massive dumping.

The brokerage, which suffered huge losses from selling short in a rising market, was later condemned by officials for willfully violating rules and manipulating the market and was merged with the former Shanghai Shenyin Securities.
Guan had also previously held the posts of president of the Shanghai Wanguo Real Estate Development Corp and board chairman of the Shanghai Wanguo (Hong Kong) Co, Xinhua said but gave no details.
